items.fullText: 전국 성안당, 일잘러 되는 실무용 '코덱스 바이브 코딩' 출간 발행일 : 2026-11-20 17:49 전자신문을 선호 매체로 추가 공유하기 페이스북 X(트위터) X(트위터) --> 메일 URL 복사 글자크기 설정 가 작게 가 보통 가 크게 코덱스 바이브 코딩 표지. 도서출판 성안당은 코딩 경험이 전혀 없어도 오픈AI의 인공지능(AI) 코딩 에이전트 '코덱스(Codex)'로 말(프롬프트나 명령어)로 지시하는 것만으로 필요한 도구를 만들 수 있는 바이브 코딩 실무서 '코덱스 바이브 코딩'을 출간했다. 특히 직장인들이라면 누구나 꼭 필요로 하는 점심 메뉴 추천 앱과 아파트 실거래가 앱, 주식 시세 대시보드 앱 등 생활 감각 있는 예제를 바이브 코딩으로 만들어 흥미를 끈다. 이 책에서는 채팅 창에서 코드를 받아도 어디에 붙여넣고 어떻게 실행해야 할지 막막했던 독자를 위해 코덱스가 답변을 내놓는 데 그치지 않고 사용자 컴퓨터의 작업 폴더에서 파일을 직접 만들고, 고치고, 실행한다. 또 익숙한 ChatGPT 데스크톱 앱에서 코덱스를 먼저 써 본 뒤 'Codex CLI'로 자연스럽게 넘어가도록 구성해 터미널이 낯선 독자도 흐름을 놓치지 않게 했다. 총 3부 18장과 부록 구성으로, 1부에서는 '오늘 점심을 골라 주는 앱'을 한 문장 요청으로 만들며 '요청하고, 만들어지고, 실행하고, 고치는' 기본 흐름을 익힌다. 2부에서는 아파트 실거래가 조회 앱을 설계부터 완성까지 키운다. 제품 요구사항 문서(PRD)와 계획 기능(/plan)으로 범위를 먼저 정하고, 코덱스가 지킬 규칙을 AGENTS.md 파일에 남기며, 샌드박스·승인 정책으로 작업 경계를 정한다. 이어 공공데이터포털 API를 연결해 실제 거래 데이터를 불러오고, 긴 작업 세션 관리와 서브 에이전트 활용법까지 다룬다. 3부에서는 국내 주식 시장 흐름을 보여 주는 대시보드를 실제 서비스 수준으로 완성한다. 실 시세 데이터 수집, MCP를 통한 데이터베이스(Supabase) 연결, Vercel 배포, 훅(Hook)을 이용한 자동 검증과 인증 키 보호, 반복 점검을 묶은 'Skill' 제작, 깃 워크트리를 활용한 동시 개발, 다음 작업자를 위한 인수인계 문서 작성까지 담았다. 부록으로는 HyperFrames와 Remotion으로 '내 아이디어에 예고편 붙이는 영상 만들기'를 수록했다. 책 전체를 관통하는 기준인 “Vibe로 만들었지만, Vibe로 믿지는 않는다.”에 맞게 코덱스가 “완료했다.”고 답하더라도 독자가 직접 프로그램을 실행하고, 화면에 나온 숫자가 어디서 온 값인지 따지고, 조건을 바꿔도 결과가 맞는지 확인하도록 안내한다. 저자 5인은 금융권과 인터넷 기업에서 서비스를 개발해 온 현직 개발자로, 앞서 '클로드 코드 바이브 코딩'을 함께 썼으며 실제 업무에서 매일 코덱스를 쓰며 얻은 경험을 책에 녹였다. 저자들은 서문에서 “'이런 것이 있으면 좋겠다.'는 생각이 들 때 작게 만들어 보고 직접 확인하는 습관을 이 책에서 얻었으면 한다.”고 밝혔다. 전남광주=김한식 기자 hskim@etnews.com

items.t: Anthropic is about to be worth more than $1 trillion. What that means for the rest of us.
items.d: Leading AI lab Anthropic is expected to make the largest-ever public market debut when it starts trading on the Nasdaq stock exchange Thursday.
items.fullText: Artificial intelligence Another AI company is about to be worth more than $1 trillion. What that means for the rest of us. Anthropic’s public market debut comes as the AI investment boom stands at a crossroads. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Anthropic co-founder and CEO Dario Amodei in Washington, in September. Finn Gomez / Getty Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 18, 2026, 4:13 PM EST / Updated Nov. 18, 2026, 4:23 PM EST By Rob Wile Leading AI lab Anthropic is expected to make the largest-ever public market debut when it starts trading on the Nasdaq stock exchange Thursday. Founded in 2021 by brother and sister Dario and Daniela Amodei, both former employees of rival OpenAI, Anthropic and its main product, Claude, are seen as the gold standard of AI models, despite lacking the household name cache of ChatGPT. With a target market value of $1.5 trillion — larger than SpaceX’s record setting IPO just a few months ago — Anthropic’s public arrival will serve as more than just a measure of what Wall Street thinks the company is worth. It will be a test of current sentiment around AI itself at a pivotal moment for the industry. For much of the past year, the AI investment wave has powered the stock market to new heights and sustained U.S. economic growth. But there are signs the wave may be starting to break. “Investors have over recent weeks become increasingly concerned around the sustainability of the investment boom,” James McCann, senior economist for investment strategy at Edward Jones, said in a client note Wednesday ahead of Anthropic’s debut. The market gains notched in the spring and summer thanks to the AI boom have now largely been wiped out. Fears of overspending on infrastructure, rising debt loads, ballooning costs and uncertain demand have grown. New NVIDIA RTX Spark compact desktops from ASUS, Dell and MSI are available today, bringing local AI agents, image and video generation, and model fine-tuning to a dedicated Windows PC. With up to 128GB of unified memory and NVIDIA’s AI software stack, these systems provide room for larger local models alongside RTX-accelerated creative and development tools. A dedicated desktop can keep agents and scheduled tasks running while a laptop travels or handles other work. Alongside the new desktops, an expanding software ecosystem brings more creative and development workflows to RTX Spark laptops and compact desktops. Native Windows on Arm applications from Adobe, the NVIDIA DLSS Ray Reconstruction feature in Blender and local generation workflows in ComfyUI expand what creators and developers can do on RTX Spark — all on one Windows PC. A Windows PC Built for Local AI As workflows expand to include local AI models and agents, more work can continue beyond an active editing session — from generating assets to processing long renders or scheduled tasks. RTX Spark compact desktops give developers, creators and AI enthusiasts a dedicated Windows PC for local models and always-on agents. They bring together image and video generation, model fine-tuning, creative applications and development tools in one compact system. Running supported models locally keeps locally processed code and files on the PC and avoids per-token cloud application programming interface (API) charges for those tasks. items.fullText: Ian Buck Kicks Off NVIDIA’s Week at SC26 as Science Enters the Age of Agents At SC26, NVIDIA’s VP of Hyperscale and HPC laid out how researchers can combine simulation, AI and agents to accelerate scientific discovery. November 17, 2026 by Brian Caulfield 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! NVIDIA’s Ian Buck kicked off the company’s week at SC26 in Chicago on Monday with new tools for AI agents, software that can plan experiments, run code and check results on researchers’ own systems. In NVIDIA’s special address, Buck announced Nemotron for Science , the Rubin HPC GPU and an expanded Vera CPU platform for high-performance computing . He also detailed a new collaboration in quantum computing with IBM and Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory . “The frontier of computing and the new scientific stack is going to be simulation, as always, but combined with AI and the future of quantum,” said Buck, vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing at NVIDIA. Buck opened the talk by looking back to his first public talk on CUDA, at an SC06 tutorial in Tampa, Florida, 20 years ago. NVIDIA now offers more than 1,000 CUDA-X libraries , he said. Open Models for Science Agents “[Agents] have been just a game changer in how we interface with our supercomputers, with our devices, our instruments and how we can do the research,” Buck said. Simulation remains the foundation of scientific computing, “which will always be on the top,” Buck said, with AI, quantum and now agents working alongside it. Nemotron for Science combines the Nemotron 3.5 Super VL open model with a new open chemistry dataset and post-training recipes for life sciences and chemistry, Buck explained. Researchers can run it locally on a DGX Spark, a workstation or their own supercomputer. In its MLPerf benchmarks debut, with results released today, the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform delivers leading performance across training, post-training and agentic inference. NVIDIA swept every MLPerf Training v6.1 benchmark and, in its first MLPerf Endpoints submission, delivered more than 10x generational gains in throughput per watt for agentic AI — measuring how much agentic work a system delivers with each watt of power. These results are just the beginning. Vera Rubin performance will keep climbing through continuous optimization of NVIDIA’s CUDA-powered software stack , so the infrastructure that customers invest in today delivers more value over time. NVIDIA Sweeps MLPerf Training v6.1 AI agents are now everywhere, writing code, running business workflows, answering customer questions and, as this week’s SC26 conference highlights , advancing scientific research. Faster training means smarter agents can reach users sooner, drug discovery models can keep pace with new lab data and fraud-detection models can adapt to new threats faster. MLPerf Training measures how fast a system can train a range of AI models to a target level of accuracy. The NVIDIA platform was the only one with results on every benchmark this round, spanning large language models, image generation, recommender systems and reinforcement learning post-training. In its debut, Vera Rubin NVL72 delivered up to 2x more performance per GPU than the highly optimized NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 system — early results that show the pace of generation-over-generation innovation. items.fullText: NVIDIA CUDA-X Libraries Give Agents the Tools to Accelerate Scientific Discovery November 16, 2026 by Kibibi Moseley 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! With expanded NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries, including cuPhoton, cuPotential and cuSpa, researchers can sift through vast amounts of data to accelerate research, from astrophysics and materials science to single-cell biology. The speedups are helping scientists analyze larger datasets and model more complex systems. The new libraries give AI agents the tools to help researchers make discoveries faster than ever. Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 Bringing Black Holes Into Focus Seeing a black hole takes a telescope the size of Earth. The Event Horizon Telescope links radio dishes worldwide, generating petabytes of data that can take months to process. With NVIDIA cuPhoton.xBeam, a module within the cuPhoton Toolkit , black hole observations from the Event Horizon Telescope can now be correlated orders of magnitude faster than ever. Analysis that once took over a month now takes eight minutes. By combining global radio dishes into Earth-sized aperture, cuPhoton delivers unprecedented astronomical imaging resolution. cuPhoton successfully correlated observations of powerful black hole jets J1924 and 3C279 in the night sky — making it a reality to reconstruct a Messier 87* black hole galaxy in real time. The entire pipeline, from data loading and processing to visualization, runs on distributed multi-GPU systems or a compact NVIDIA DGX Spark system, helping scientists study how gas spirals inward under a black hole’s powerful gravitational pull. Steering Fusion Simulations Sustaining plasma at millions of degrees is essential to achieving stable, continuous fusion energy. But simulating its behavior is costly: on petascale systems, a single time step can take days, with simulations running for weeks. items.fullText: AI Day Seoul Brings Together Korea’s Industry Leaders, Startups and Developer Communities November 15, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Over two days at COEX, more than 2,000 attendees converged for AI Day Seoul, bringing together Korea’s industry leaders, startups and developer communities advancing physical AI and AI agents. At the plenary sessions, Deepu Talla, vice president of robotics and edge AI at NVIDIA, said Korea is “punching above its weight,” with Doosan Robotics, Hyundai Motor Group, LG Electronics and SK Group — as well as startups like Real World and Luda Robotics — using NVIDIA platforms to bring general-purpose robotics into the real world. Jonathan Cohen, vice president of applied research at NVIDIA, showed how enterprises can build agents they own and control. Breakout sessions featured speakers from Coupang Intelligent Cloud, Doosan Robotics, LG AI Research, LG Electronics, NAVER Cloud, SK Telecom and Upstage. “It was a genuinely enjoyable time to have candid conversations,” said Hyunho Yang, research engineer for omnimodal foundation models at SK Telecom. “Seeing the passion of fellow AI developers was a real source of inspiration for me.” Community leaders share how they build with open models and tools at AI Day Seoul. The Agentic AI 10x Bootcamp Community Day brought together Pseudo Lab, Python Korea, PyTorchKR, HAERAE, Hugging Face KREW, Graph User Group, Womxn Who Code Korea, Dnol (Datayanolja) and other developer communities. Five finalists from the Hangul Day hackathon, co-hosted with Fastcampus, built agents trained on the Korean language and culture with the OpenShell runtime. The winning team, FlyGate, received an NVIDIA DGX Spark system. More than 500 developers also took part in full-day NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute workshops and NVIDIA Certification exams in Korean.
